# Register your interest in our dog cancer trial

We are recruiting dogs with mast cell cancer in Australia for an investigational trial of personalised mRNA cancer vaccines. Register your interest and share a few details about your dog. Our team will contact you about further screening.

Why we are running this trial

## From Rosie’s story to a future for more dogs.

Image: Rosie

Rosie

The first dog treated with a personalised neoantigen vaccine.

It began with Rosie. Her experience with a personalised neoantigen vaccine encouraged Paul to explore how this approach could one day be made available to every dog with cancer.

Before an approach like this can become broadly available, we must study it carefully and support it by evidence for review by the relevant veterinary regulators. This clinical trial is an important step in that process, helping us learn from participating dogs and understand the vaccine more fully.

Read Rosie’s personalised mRNA cancer-vaccine story  →

Who can register

## If your dog has cancer and is currently in Australia, you’re welcome to register your interest. Our team will check whether your dog may be eligible for this trial.

Register your interest  →

About the trial

## What this trial is looking at

The trial will investigate a personalised mRNA vaccine approach for dogs with mast cell cancer. Tell us about your dog and our team will help determine whether they may be eligible for screening.

Image

### Who can register

Dogs diagnosed with mast cell cancer who are based in, or able to travel within, Australia.

Every case is reviewed individually

Image

### The trial approach

A therapeutic mRNA vaccine designed from each dog’s own tumour and blood samples, intended to work alongside—not replace—existing care.

Personalised to each dog

Image

### What screening involves

We help coordinate records, screening, sample logistics and updates, working with the trial team and your treating veterinarian.

A named team stays in touch

Trial registration and screening

## How to register your interest.

You don’t need to have every record ready before registering your interest. Start with what you know and we’ll help with the rest.

01

### Register your interest

Complete a short form with basic details about your dog, their mast cell cancer diagnosis and where you live.

02

### We get in touch

A Gamgee coordinator will contact you, answer practical questions and—with your permission—help gather relevant records from your vet.

03

### The trial team confirms eligibility

The authorised study team and treating veterinarian assess potential eligibility. If your dog may proceed, you’ll receive the approved trial information and consent discussion before deciding.

These are indicative timings from a single case. Sequencing turnaround and manufacturing schedules may vary. We will give you a case-specific estimate before proceeding.

## Ready to tell us about your dog?

Registering your interest does not guarantee eligibility or enrolment. Please continue your dog's existing veterinary care while your information is reviewed.

Register your interest  →

A University of Queensland project could be a glimmer of hope for dogs suffering from inoperable or incurable cancers.

The project will test the effectiveness of immunomodulatory drug Enzistat in treating solid tumours caused by naturally occurring cancers, including soft tissue sarcoma, mast cell tumour and melanoma.

Professor Rachel Allavena from UQ’s School of Veterinary Science said owners who had been told their dog’s cancer was terminal or their pet’s tumours were inoperable should apply for the trial.

“The 6-week treatment consists of oral tablet Enzistat being administered twice daily, regular consultations, blood samples and biopsies,” Professor Allavena said.

Dr Jose Granados Soler said canine cancers could be treated with surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy but expense and availability often prevented dogs receiving treatment.

“Immunotherapeutics is in its infancy in veterinary medicine and is a newly established approach in human oncology,” Dr Granados Soler said.

“Our goal is to develop safe, easily applied immunotherapies, amenable to delivery in general practice at an affordable cost.

“We will optimise these therapies as sole or combination with standard of care treatments, giving each pet dog the best chance to fight its cancer.”

UQ is undertaking this trial in partnership with drug discovery company Avammune Therapeutics Inc that developed Enzistat.

Avammune Therapeutics chief executive Arun Papaiah said beginning the first formal veterinary clinical trial with The University of Queensland was a monumental step.

“This trial is not just about advancing science, it’s about providing families more time with their beloved companions,” Mr Papaiah said.

“Enzistat is designed to be an oral, off-the-shelf drug that provides high-end immunotherapy results without the complexity of hospital-based infusions.”

The trial will provide Enzistat and research associated assessments, with participants required to cover other veterinary costs.

Owners of eligible dogs should apply for the trial by contacting uqvets.sa@uq.edu.au.

### Has your dog recently undergone spleen removal for haemangiosarcoma? Join our clinical trial combining immunotherapy with chemotherapy.

MediPaws is participating in a multi-centre clinical trial, led by the University of Melbourne, investigating a novel treatment approach for dogs with splenic haemangiosarcoma. This study evaluates the use of an autologous tumour vaccine (a personalised vaccine made from your dog’s own tumour) in combination with standard chemotherapy (doxorubicin).

This research has been reviewed and approved by the University of Melbourne Animal Ethics Committee (Project ID 35274).

# Why participate?

### Helping advance treatment for haemangiosarcoma

This study is exploring whether stimulating the immune system alongside chemotherapy can improve outcomes for dogs with this aggressive cancer.

### Meaningful benefits for your dog

Dogs enrolled in the study will receive:

  * Standard-of-care chemotherapy with a veterinary oncologist
  * Access to a personalised tumour vaccine at no cost
  * Close monitoring by a specialist oncology team
  * Contribution to research that may improve future treatment options

### Eligibility

Dogs may be eligible if they:

  * Have a confirmed diagnosis of splenic haemangiosarcoma
  * Have undergone splenectomy (surgical removal of the spleen)
  * Have no visible evidence of metastatic disease prior to starting chemotherapy
  * Are planned to receive doxorubicin chemotherapy

Eligibility is confirmed by Dr Sonya Yu,  the MediPaws oncologist.

# What’s involved?

### What happens in the study?

Your dog will receive standard chemotherapy as planned. The study adds a personalised vaccine created from the original tumour tissue.

Treatment and monitoring are performed alongside routine oncology care.

### Participation requirements

There are no major additional procedures beyond standard treatment and follow-up.

Participation is voluntary, and you may withdraw at any time.

# Costs

The autologous vaccine is provided free of charge.

Standard veterinary care, including chemotherapy and associated costs, are not covered by the study.

# Interested in enrolling?

MediPaws is actively enrolling dogs into this clinical trial.

If you think your dog may be eligible, we recommend contacting MediPaws directly or speaking with your veterinarian to discuss suitability and next steps.

Our oncology team can guide you through eligibility, treatment planning, and enrolment.

## Kv9 Pilot Study

Purpose of study: 

To assess efficacy and safety of Kv9 across a range of solid tumours. 

Eligible tumour types: 

  * Soft tissue sarcomas 

  * Mast cell tumours 

  * Mammary gland tumours

  * Melanomas 

  * Anal gland tumours 

  * Squamous cell carcinomas 

  * Other tumours may be considered 

Primary eligibility criteria*: ​

  * Tumour type diagnosed by fine needle aspirate or biopsy by a registered veterinary pathologist 

  * ​Tumour smaller than 5cm 

  * Not receiving immune modulatory drugs

    * It is acceptable to be taking/receiving including apoquel, cytopoint, beranza or a recent vaccination 

  * No wounds on the surface of soft tissue sarcoma tumours

    * Other tumour types will be a case by case basis ​

*See referral form for complete criteria ​

Study protocol: 

  1. Primary veterinarian to send through referral for assessment by Kode Veterinary Sciences (KVS). 

  2. Additional testing completed as required. 

  3. Atleast two treatment appointments to receive Kv9 at treatment centres.

  4. A minimum of 9 revisits at primary care veterinarian or treatment centres over 2 years. 

Owner responsibilities: 

  * You are responsible to schedule and attend all required visits  ​

  * You are responsible for the initial costs to diagnose your dogs tumour, and any other tests recommended by your veterinarian  

  * You are responsible to closely monitor your pet for any changes and update the clinical study team in a timely manner 

Financial support: 

  * There is no cost to participate in the clinical study. KVS will cover the cost of treatment and monitoring appointments, and provide the Kv9 treatment free of charge. 

  * KVS will provide support to any participant experiencing adverse events during their time in the trial. If the event is suspected to be related to the Kv9 treatment, KVS will provide financial support, unless agreed to be excluded in the consent form.

Overview

Japan Small Animal Medical Center Foundation (Tokorozawa, Saitama), Yamaguchi University Joint Faculty of Veterinary Medicine (Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi), and Kamogawa Animal Medical Center (Kyoto, Kyoto), in collaboration with Nippon Zenyaku Kogyo Co., Ltd., are launching a corporate clinical trial of an “anti-canine PD-1 antibody” for canine oral malignant melanoma. This trial aims to obtain approval as a veterinary pharmaceutical product and will be conducted at three facilities: the Japan Small Animal Cancer Center (affiliated with the Japan Small Animal Medical Center), the Animal Medical Center (affiliated with the Yamaguchi University Joint Faculty of Veterinary Medicine), and Kamogawa Animal Medical Center.

## 臨床試験について

本院で行っている、もしくは行う予定の臨床試験についてです。臨床試験とは、安全で有効となりうることが期待される医薬品もしくは医療機器を用いた治療です。 飼い主様への十分な説明と、飼い主様の同意の下で実施します。現在実施している臨床試験は以下の通りです。

  * 慢性腸症罹患犬に対する乳酸菌およびオリゴ糖の有効性に関する臨床試験
  * 犬の組織球性肉腫に対する抗PD-1抗体を用いた臨床試験
  * 犬猫の固形腫瘍に対するがんオルガノイドスクリーニング検査に基づく分子標的薬投与の安全性と有効性検証のための臨床試験
  * ネコの移行上皮癌に対するラパチニブの獣医師主導臨床試験
  * 犬の膀胱・尿道移行上皮癌および前立腺癌に対する臨床試験
  * 犬の膀胱癌に対するIDO1阻害剤の臨床試験

犬の組織球性肉腫は極めて悪性の癌であり、急速に進行することが知られていますが有効な治療法は確立されていません。
近年、人においてPD-1という分子を標的とした抗体薬を用いた免疫療法が、がん患者の一部で有効であることがわかってきました。また犬においても山口大学のこれまでの臨床試験によりある種のがんに対して効果があることが明らかとなりました。
そこで、あらたに犬の組織球肉腫に対する犬PD-1に対する抗体薬の有効性と安全性を調べるために、臨床試験を実施しています。なお、この試験は2026年7月に当センター臨床試験委員会において倫理的承認を受けております。

### 対象(抜粋)

  * 当センターでの生検から組織球性肉腫と診断されること
  * 生検後も各種検査で病変が検出されること
  * 免疫抑制剤投与や免疫療法を受けていないこと
  * 当センターへの定期的な通院が可能であること

※このほかにも複数の基準があります。特に、大型犬の場合は必ずしも参加できない可能性があることをご了承ください。

### 内容 (抜粋)

  * 当センターにて組織生検による確定診断を実施します。
  * 臨床試験内容の詳細を説明し、参加の意思を確認します。
  * 参加していただく場合は試験薬を2週間に一回静脈内投与し、その効果と副作用を当院にて確認します。

ご協力いただける方は下記連絡先(当センター受付)までご連絡ください。
＜問い合わせ先＞
東京大学大学院 農学生命科学研究科

  * 治療効果検証のための病変の採材にご協力頂ける飼い主様

  * ご自宅にて内服薬を投与していただきます。

  * 当院受診時には、一般検査(身体検査、血液検査、画像検査など)を実施し、有効性や安全性の評価をします。

### 抗PD-L1抗体による腫瘍免疫療法について（臨床研究）

本院では、北海道大学獣医学研究院にて開発したイヌ用抗体医薬「抗PD-L1抗体」によるイヌの腫瘍疾患の試験的治療（臨床研究）を行っており、研究へ参加していただける患者さんを募集しています。

本治療薬は免疫チェックポイント阻害剤と呼ばれる新しい免疫療法薬であり、ヒト医療における抗PD-1抗体（ニボルマブ、ペンブロリズマブ）や抗PD-L1抗体（アテゾリズマブ、デュルバルマブ）と同様の作用機序を持ちます。

### Kv9 intratumoral immunotherapy pilot for accessible solid tumors

Kode Veterinary Sciences — New Zealand multicentre pilot · New Zealand

Recruiting — current official pilot page and owner FAQ

What is being offered: Intratumoral Kv9 immunotherapy, usually up to three treatments about two weeks apart, followed by at least nine monitoring visits over two years

Who may qualify: Confirmed cancer diagnosis required; Active tumor required; Measurable; Accessible intratumoral target; Min tumor cm: 1; Max tumor cm: 5; Kv9 concurrent drugs eligible

May not qualify if: Concurrent chemotherapy

Costs / coverage: Kv9, treatment appointments and study monitoring visits are covered. Owners pay the initial tumor diagnosis and other veterinarian-recommended tests. Unrelated care, pre-existing conditions and agreed exclusions remain owner-paid; travel coverage is not stated.

Contact: Kode Veterinary Sciences clinical study team — study@kodevet9.com; referral through the primary veterinarian
